quote.text: In every walk with nature, one receives far more than he seeks.
quote.author: John Muir

fun_fact.text: Hummingbirds are the only birds that can fly backwards! They can also hover in place by flapping their wings in a figure-eight pattern up to 80 times per second. September is a wonderful time to see them in the Pacific Northwest as they fuel up before their long migration south.

short_read.title: The Secret Language of Trees
short_read.teaser: Scientists have discovered that trees communicate with each other through an underground network of fungi, sharing nutrients and warning signals. It's like a natural internet connecting the forest!

medium_read.title: The Hidden History of America's Victory Gardens
medium_read.teaser: During World War II, American families grew over 40% of the nation's vegetables in backyard victory gardens. This heartwarming story shows how communities came together through gardening, creating beauty and abundance even in difficult times.

long_read.title: The Return of Wolves to Yellowstone
long_read.teaser: When wolves were reintroduced to Yellowstone National Park after 70 years, something magical happened—the entire ecosystem transformed in unexpected ways. This is the remarkable story of how one species can heal an entire landscape.

port_angeles.title: Harbor Seal Pupping Season Winds Down
port_angeles.description: September is the tail end of harbor seal pupping season along the Strait of Juan de Fuca. You might still spot mothers with their pups resting on the rocks near Ediz Hook or along the shoreline. Remember to keep a respectful distance—at least 100 yards—so these wonderful marine mammals feel safe.

puzzle_1.question: A hummingbird's heart beats approximately ___ times per minute while in flight.
puzzle_1.correct_response: That's exactly right, Barbara! Amazing that such a tiny heart can beat so fast!
puzzle_1.close_response: You're very close! Their heart beats about 1,200 times per minute—incredibly fast for such a tiny bird!
puzzle_1.wrong_response: Their heart actually beats about 1,200 times per minute! That's about 20 beats every single second—no wonder they need so much nectar for energy!
puzzle_1.learn_more_text: A hummingbird's heart rate can slow to 250 beats per minute when they go into torpor at night to conserve energy. This incredible adaptation helps them survive cool nights when food isn't available.

puzzle_2.question: Which Hungarian word means 'butterfly'?
puzzle_2.correct_response: Wonderful, Barbara! Pillangó is such a beautiful word for such a beautiful creature!
puzzle_2.wrong_response: The Hungarian word for butterfly is 'pillangó'—such a lovely, musical word! (Madár means bird, virág means flower, and napraforgó means sunflower.)
puzzle_2.learn_more_text: Hungarian is unique among European languages because it's part of the Finno-Ugric language family, making it related to Finnish and Estonian rather than other neighboring languages. Many Hungarian words have a musical, flowing quality.

puzzle_3.question: What type of tree is the most common in Olympic National Park's temperate rainforests?
puzzle_3.correct_response: Perfect! Sitka spruce trees thrive in the misty valleys of the Olympic rainforest, growing to truly magnificent sizes in that perfect, wet climate.
puzzle_3.wrong_response: It's actually the Sitka spruce! These magnificent trees can grow over 300 feet tall in the Hoh and Quinault rainforests, draped with moss and ferns in those magical, misty valleys.
puzzle_3.learn_more_text: The Sitka spruce in Olympic National Park can live for over 700 years and create cathedral-like groves. The temperate rainforest receives 12-14 feet of rain annually, creating one of the most lush ecosystems on Earth.
